canonicalJson.whyNotMerged: Merging would change an output or a refusal, not every digest. Of the 1,439 production lenient calls the full suite made, 685 are spelled alike by the strict encoder and 754 are not: 753 carry an undefined member (lenient drops it, strict refuses with unsupported-value) and 1 a BigInt (both refuse, with different errors). Three PWB identities are spelled identically by both on every observed call (canonicalManifestJson 299 of 299, resourceLimitsDigest 272 of 272, walkthroughEvaluationIdentity 11 of 11); the two with differing calls are observeProjectShapeSources (190 of 271) and buildResponseIdentity (564 of 586). The only value class on which the two disagree without either refusing is the array-index key order (31 of 600 in population B); no production call was seen to carry one. 754 of 1,439 is 52.4 percent of the lenient calls the suite made; the value of a call may still be a test fixture. Superseded: the round-1 text said a merge would change the digests of every PWB identity and refuse about 52 percent of the calls (review note N1); the tap does not show the first.

residuals: withoutGitlinkRecords in code-structure.ts runs inside the try that converts any throw to NonUtf8GitOutput, as the decode always did. It throws only when Buffer.concat cannot allocate the copy of the kept records, up to the 256 MiB maxBuffer [Inferred: from the code; it calls indexOf, subarray and equals, none of which throws on content]. The caller then reports Unknown with the reason "code-structure observation produced a path that is not valid UTF-8", which is the base reason; [Inferred] it is not the truer one for an allocation failure, and changing it is a refusal-string change for the owner, not made here. Both arms are pinned by an injected Buffer.concat failure (code-structure.test.ts). The reviewed head (2d3f9375) ran the filter outside the try and reported "repository or revision was unreadable during code-structure observation" for the same fault (review F2).

decode-utf8.ts constructs its TextDecoder at module load. On a Node built without ICU the constructor throws ERR_NO_ICU for the fatal option [Observed by the review in the embedded lib/internal/encoding.js of Node v24.6.0; not re-run here, this host's Node has ICU 77.1], so importing @syzygy/support throws; [Inferred, by the review] at the base the consent, policy and registry readers built their decoder inside their try and refused every artifact as "not strict UTF-8", and the other sites failed only at their first decode. Both fail closed; official Node builds ship ICU. Constructing the decoder lazily would change this and is not done here (review N6).
